STEP 1: halb looks ahead to the next hour. Halb vier is half an hour BEFORE four: 3:30, not "half four".
Four traps are waiting for English speakers — and one of them can make you an hour late.
De 21 a 99 o alemão lê primeiro a unidad: From 21 to 99, German says the ones first and then the tens, joined by «und»: 25 = fünfundzwanzig, "five-and-twenty" — like the old English "four-and-twenty blackbirds". «Eins» becomes «ein»: 21 = einundzwanzig. And it's all one word. Watch 16 and 60 (sechzehn, sechzig) and 17 and 70 (siebzehn, siebzig): they drop letters. 30 is dreißig, with ß. Hundreds simply add up: zweihundert (200), 101 = hunderteins. A thousand is «tausend». Phone numbers are usually read digit by digit.

Perguntas: «Wie spät ist es?» ou «Wie vi: Questions: «Wie spät ist es?» or «Wie viel Uhr ist es?» (What time is it?). Answer: «Es ist acht Uhr.» For the time something happens: «Um wie viel Uhr?» — «Um acht Uhr» (at eight). In everyday speech: «fünf nach acht» (8:05, five past eight), «Viertel nach acht» (8:15, quarter past), «halb neun» (8:30), «Viertel vor neun» (8:45, quarter to), «fünf vor neun» (8:55). Careful: «halb neun» means HALF AN HOUR BEFORE nine, so 8:30. British "half nine" means 9:30 — the opposite! In official contexts (trains, TV) the 24-hour clock is used: «acht Uhr dreißig», «vierzehn Uhr fünfzehn».
em português «oito e meia» olha para a h: English "half past eight" looks back at the hour that has passed. German «halb neun» looks ahead to the hour that's coming, nine. «Viertel nach» and «Viertel vor» work just like "quarter past" and "quarter to".

Dias da semana, meses e a data: Days of the week, months and the date
Os dias da semana e os meses são todos m: Days and months are all masculine (der Montag, der Januar) — and like all nouns, capitalized. «Am» + day = on (Monday): «am Montag». «Im» + month = in (January): «im Mai». The date uses an ordinal with a period: «der 5. Oktober» (der fünfte Oktober) — the period does the job of English "th". Up to 19, the ordinal is the number + -te (der vierte); 1, 3, 7 and 8 are special (erste, dritte, siebte, achte), as in first, third. From 20 on, it's the number + -ste (der zwanzigste). In «am 5. Oktober», read «am fünften Oktober». The day comes before the month: 5.10. is October 5th.

Einundzwanzig significa 21: ein represen: Einundzwanzig means 21: ein is the ones, und joins the parts and zwanzig is the tens. From 21 to 99, the ones come before the tens.
Dreißig significa 30. Não confunda com d: Dreißig means 30. Don't confuse it with dreizehn, 13: in dreißig, -ßig is the tens ending (like English -ty).
Halb vier indica meia hora antes das qua: Halb vier means half an hour before four: 3:30. The hour named after halb is the next hour.
Viertel vor sechs indica um quarto de ho: Viertel vor sechs means a quarter to six: 5:45. Vor shows the minutes left until the next hour.
Siebte é o ordinal sétimo. Der siebte Ma: Siebte is the ordinal "seventh". Der siebte Mai is May 7th; May 17th would be der siebzehnte Mai.
